e-3362.knowledge_point: Finding the Tangent Line to a Level Curve
e-3362.problem: Given the function $f(x,y) = 6x^2+2y^2 - 2xy^2,$ find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y) = (3,3).$
e-3362.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y) = k$ at the point $(x_0,y_0)$ can be expressed as

$$
\nabla f(x_0,y_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0 \rangle  = 0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y) = (3,3)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\text{ }i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\text{ }j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(6{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-2x{y}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(6{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-2x{y}^{2})\text{ }j \\  & =(12x-2{y}^{2})\text{ }i+(4y-4xy)\text{ }j \\ ∇\,f(3,3) & =(12(3)-2(3)^{2})i+(4(3)-4(3)(3))j \\  & =18\,i-24\,j \\  & =⟨18,-24⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent to the level curve that passes through the point $(x_0,y_0)=(3,3)$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(3,3)\cdot ⟨x-3,\,y-3⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨18,-24⟩\cdot ⟨x-3,\,y-3⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We can leave our answer in this form. Or, if we want to leave our final answer in Cartesian form, we expand the dot product and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}18(x-3)-24(y-3) & =0 \\ 18x-24y+18 & =0 \\ 3x-4y+3 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070260/assets/102f55fe0add794d3ee0f9f044b5e35c4403d4f160fe36e97d737d33ef3abb68.png)

e-3363.knowledge_point: Finding a Tangent Vector to a Plane Curve
e-3363.problem: Consider the plane curve $x^2-3xy+4y=2.$ Find a tangent vector to the curve at the point $(1,1).$
e-3363.worked_solution:
First, if we set $f(x,y) = x^2-3xy+4y,$ our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=2.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(1,1)$ can be computed as follows:

$$
\mathbf t(1,1) = f_y(1,1) \ \mathbf i - f_x(1,1) \ \mathbf j
$$

So, we calculate $\mathbf t(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(1,1)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-3xy+4y)\text{ }i-\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-3xy+4y)\text{ }j \\  & =(-3x+4)\text{ }i-(2x-3y)\text{ }j \\ t(1,1) & =(-3(1)+4)\text{ }i-(2(1)-3(1))\text{ }j \\  & =1\,i-(-1)\,j \\  & =i+j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our tangent vector is $\mathbf i +\mathbf j,$ as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070260/assets/0114bf524d085402bd27178d687a5faf176b7147c8e8726b84042b17823b6b0b.png)

e-3364.knowledge_point: Finding the Points on a Curve at which the Tangent Vector is Perpendicular to a Given Vector
e-3364.problem: At which points on the curve $6xy+3y^2 =7+ y - 3x^2$ is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector $\mathbf{j}?$
e-3364.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}6xy+3{y}^{2} & =7+y-3{x}^{2} \\ 6xy+3{y}^{2}-y+3{x}^{2} & =7\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y) = 6xy+3y^2 - y + 3x^2 ,$ our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=7.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows:

$$
\mathbf t(x,y) = f_y(x,y) \ \mathbf i - f_x(x,y) \ \mathbf j
$$

So, we calculate $\mathbf t(x,y)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & ={f}_{y}(x,y)\text{ }i-{f}_{x}(x,y)\text{ }j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(6xy+3{y}^{2}-y+3{x}^{2})\,i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(6xy+3{y}^{2}-y+3{x}^{2})\,j \\  & =(6x+6y-1)\,i-(6y+6x)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to $\mathbf{j},$ we must have $\mathbf t \cdot \mathbf j = 0.$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y)\cdot j & =0 \\ ((6x+6y-1)\,i-(6y+6x)\,j)\cdot j & =0 \\ -6y-6x & =0 \\ y & =-x\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $y=-x$ into the equation of our curve gives

$$
\begin{aligned}6xy+3{y}^{2} & =7+y-3{x}^{2} \\ 6x(-x)+3(-x)^{2} & =7+(-x)-3{x}^{2} \\ -6{x}^{2}+3{x}^{2} & =7-x-3{x}^{2} \\ x & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, if $x=7,$ we get $y=-7$ and the corresponding point is $(7,-7).$

decision.explanation: The gradient is ∇f(x,y)=⟨2x−4y,−4x+10y⟩, so ∇f(−1,−1)=⟨2,−6⟩. The tangent line is therefore ⟨2,−6⟩·⟨x+1,y+1⟩=0, which is option c.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Given the function $f(x,y)={x}^{2}-4xy+5{y}^{2}$ find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(-1,-1).$
after.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(-1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-4xy+5{y}^{2})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-4xy+5{y}^{2})\,j \\  & =(2x-4y)\,i+(10y-4x)\,j \\ ∇f(-1,-1) & =(2(-1)-4(-1))\,i+(10(-1)-4(-1))\,j \\  & =2\,i-6\,j \\  & =⟨2,-6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(-1,-1)\cdot ⟨x-(-1),\,y-(-1)⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨2,-6⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y+1⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}

Question 1
?

Given the function f(x,y)=x2−4xy+5y2 find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where (x,y)=(−1,−1).

a
⟨0,−1⟩⋅⟨x+1,y+1⟩=0
b
⟨−2,4⟩⋅⟨x+1,y+1⟩=0
c
⟨2,−6⟩⋅⟨x+1,y+1⟩=0
d
⟨3,1⟩⋅⟨x+1,y+1⟩=0
e
⟨2,0⟩⋅⟨x+1,y+1⟩=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The equation of the tangent line to the level curve f(x,y)=k at the point (x0,y0) can be expressed as ∇f(x0,y0)⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0⟩=0.

First, we find the gradient of f(x,y) and evaluate it at (x,y)=(−1,−1): ∇f(x,y)=fx(x,y)i+fy(x,y)j=∂∂x(x2−4xy+5y2)i+∂∂y(x2−4xy+5y2)j=(2x−4y)i+(10y−4x)j∇f(−1,−1)=(2(−1)−4(−1))i+(10(−1)−4(−1))j=2i−6j=⟨2,−6⟩

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point (x0,y0) can be written as ∇f(x0,y0)⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0⟩=0∇f(−1,−1)⋅⟨x−(−1),y−(−1)⟩=0⟨2,−6⟩⋅⟨x+1,y+1⟩=0.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Tangent Line to a Level Curve
content.problem: Given the function $f(x,y)={x}^{2}-4xy+5{y}^{2}$ find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(-1,-1).$
content.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(-1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-4xy+5{y}^{2})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-4xy+5{y}^{2})\,j \\  & =(2x-4y)\,i+(10y-4x)\,j \\ ∇f(-1,-1) & =(2(-1)-4(-1))\,i+(10(-1)-4(-1))\,j \\  & =2\,i-6\,j \\  & =⟨2,-6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(-1,-1)\cdot ⟨x-(-1),\,y-(-1)⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨2,-6⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y+1⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 2
?

Given the function f(x,y)=2xy2+xy+2x, find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where (x,y)=(1,1).

a
⟨5,5⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−1⟩=0
b
⟨−5,5⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−1⟩=0
c
⟨2,3⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−1⟩=0
d
⟨3,2⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−1⟩=0
e
⟨4,5⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−1⟩=0
Submit

decision.explanation: The gradient is ∇f(x,y)=⟨2y²+y+2,4xy+x⟩. At (1,1), it equals ⟨5,5⟩, which is normal to the level curve. Thus the tangent line is ⟨5,5⟩·⟨x−1,y−1⟩=0.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Given the function $f(x,y)=2x{y}^{2}+xy+2x$, find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(1,1).$
after.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x{y}^{2}+xy+2x)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x{y}^{2}+xy+2x)\,j \\  & =(2{y}^{2}+y+2)\,i+(4xy+x)\,j \\ ∇\,f(1,1) & =(2(1)^{2}+(1)+2)\,i+(4(1)(1)+(1))\,j \\  & =5\,i+5\,j \\  & =⟨5,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,1)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨5,5⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Given the function f(x,y)=2xy2+xy+2x, find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where (x,y)=(1,1).

a
⟨5,5⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−1⟩=0
b
⟨−5,5⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−1⟩=0
c
⟨2,3⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−1⟩=0
d
⟨3,2⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−1⟩=0
e
⟨4,5⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−1⟩=0
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The equation of the tangent line to the level curve f(x,y)=k at the point (x0,y0) can be expressed as

∇f(x0,y0)⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0⟩=0.

First, we find the gradient of f(x,y) and evaluate it at (x,y)=(1,1):

∇f(x,y)=fx(x,y)i+fy(x,y)j=∂∂x(2xy2+xy+2x)i+∂∂y(2xy2+xy+2x)j=(2y2+y+2)i+(4xy+x)j∇f(1,1)=(2(1)2+(1)+2)i+(4(1)(1)+(1))j=5i+5j=⟨5,5⟩

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point (x0,y0) can be written as: ∇f(x0,y0)⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0⟩=0∇f(1,1)⋅⟨x−1,y−1⟩=0⟨5,5⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−1⟩=0

verification.explanation: Rechecking gives ∇f(1,1)=⟨2(1)²+1+2,4(1)(1)+1⟩=⟨5,5⟩. Thus the tangent line is ⟨5,5⟩·⟨x−1,y−1⟩=0, matching option a and the revealed solution. The displayed incorrect result concerns the deliberately submitted option d.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Tangent Line to a Level Curve
content.problem: Given the function $f(x,y)=2x{y}^{2}+xy+2x$, find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(1,1).$
content.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x{y}^{2}+xy+2x)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x{y}^{2}+xy+2x)\,j \\  & =(2{y}^{2}+y+2)\,i+(4xy+x)\,j \\ ∇\,f(1,1) & =(2(1)^{2}+(1)+2)\,i+(4(1)(1)+(1))\,j \\  & =5\,i+5\,j \\  & =⟨5,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,1)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨5,5⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Given the function f(x,y)=ln⁡(x2+y2+1), find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where (x,y)=(−1,0).

a
⟨0,−2⟩⋅⟨x+1,y⟩=0
b
⟨−1,0⟩⋅⟨x+1,y⟩=0
c
⟨−1,1⟩⋅⟨x+1,y⟩=0
d
⟨2,0⟩⋅⟨x+1,y⟩=0
e
⟨1,−1⟩⋅⟨x+1,y⟩=0
Submit

decision.explanation: ∇f(x,y)=⟨2x/(x²+y²+1),2y/(x²+y²+1)⟩, so ∇f(−1,0)=⟨−1,0⟩. The tangent line is ⟨−1,0⟩·⟨x+1,y⟩=0. Option d describes the same line x=−1, but b directly uses the gradient.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Given the function $f(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1),$ find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(-1,0).$
after.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(-1,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1))\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1))\,j \\  & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}\,i+\frac{2y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}\,j \\ ∇f(-1,0) & =\frac{2(-1)}{(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}+1}\,i+\frac{2(0)}{(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}+1}\,j \\  & =(-1)i+0\,j \\  & =⟨-1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(-1,0)\cdot ⟨x-(-1),\,y-0⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-1,0⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Tangent Line to a Level Curve
content.problem: Given the function $f(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1),$ find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(-1,0).$
content.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(-1,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1))\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1))\,j \\  & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}\,i+\frac{2y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}\,j \\ ∇f(-1,0) & =\frac{2(-1)}{(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}+1}\,i+\frac{2(0)}{(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}+1}\,j \\  & =(-1)i+0\,j \\  & =⟨-1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(-1,0)\cdot ⟨x-(-1),\,y-0⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-1,0⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Given the function f(x,y)=xy2−x+y, find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where (x,y)=(1,−1).

a
⟨−1,1⟩⋅⟨x−1,y+1⟩=0
b
⟨1,0⟩⋅⟨x−1,y+1⟩=0
c
⟨0,−1⟩⋅⟨x−1,y+1⟩=0
d
⟨−1,0⟩⋅⟨x−1,y+1⟩=0
e
⟨1,−1⟩⋅⟨x−1,y+1⟩=0
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The equation of the tangent line to the level curve f(x,y)=k at the point (x0,y0) can be expressed as ∇f(x0,y0)⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0⟩=0.

First, we find the gradient of f(x,y) and evaluate it at (x,y)=(1,−1): ∇f(x,y)=fx(x,y)i+fy(x,y)j=∂∂x(xy2−x+y)i+∂∂y(xy2−x+y)j=(y2−1) i+(2xy+1) j∇f(1,−1)=((−1)2−1)i+(2(1)(−1)+1)j=0i−j=⟨0,−1⟩

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point (x0,y0) can be written as ∇f(x0,y0)⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0⟩=0∇f(1,−1)⋅⟨x−1,y−(−1)⟩=0⟨0,−1⟩⋅⟨x−1,y+1⟩=0.

verification.explanation: Rechecking, ∇f(x,y)=⟨y²−1,2xy+1⟩ gives ∇f(1,−1)=⟨0,−1⟩. Thus the tangent line is ⟨0,−1⟩·⟨x−1,y+1⟩=0, matching option c and the revealed solution. The incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option b.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Tangent Line to a Level Curve
content.problem: Given the function $f(x,y)=x{y}^{2}-x+y,$ find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(1,-1).$
content.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{2}-x+y)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{2}-x+y)\,j \\  & =({y}^{2}-1)\text{ }i+(2xy+1)\text{ }j \\ ∇f(1,-1) & =((-1)^{2}-1)\,i+(2(1)(-1)+1)\,j \\  & =0\,i-j \\  & =⟨0,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,-1)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-(-1)⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨0,-1⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y+1⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Given the function f(x,y)=x2y2+xy, find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where (x,y)=(1,2).

a
⟨15,10⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−2⟩=0
b
⟨10,5⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−2⟩=0
c
⟨5,10⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−2⟩=0
d
⟨8,5⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−2⟩=0
e
⟨−10,15⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−2⟩=0
Submit

decision.explanation: The gradient is ∇f(x,y)=⟨2xy²+y,2x²y+x⟩. At (1,2), it equals ⟨10,5⟩, so the tangent line is ⟨10,5⟩·⟨x−1,y−2⟩=0.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Given the function $f(x,y)={x}^{2}{y}^{2}+xy$, find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(1,2).$
after.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as 

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(1,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}+xy)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}+xy)\,j \\  & =(2x{y}^{2}+y)\,i+(2y{x}^{2}+x)\,j \\ ∇\,f(1,2) & =(2(1)(2)^{2}+(2))\,i+(2(2)(1)^{2}+(1))\,j \\  & =10\,i+5\,j \\  & =⟨10,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,2)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-2⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨10,5⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-2⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Tangent Line to a Level Curve
content.problem: Given the function $f(x,y)={x}^{2}{y}^{2}+xy$, find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(1,2).$
content.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as 

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(1,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}+xy)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}+xy)\,j \\  & =(2x{y}^{2}+y)\,i+(2y{x}^{2}+x)\,j \\ ∇\,f(1,2) & =(2(1)(2)^{2}+(2))\,i+(2(2)(1)^{2}+(1))\,j \\  & =10\,i+5\,j \\  & =⟨10,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,2)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-2⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨10,5⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-2⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: Consider the plane curve $x\operatorname{cos}⁡y=-y\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{\pi }{2}.$ Find a tangent vector to that curve at the point $(\frac{\pi }{2},0).$
after.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\operatorname{cos}⁡y & =-y\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{\pi }{2} \\ x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+y\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =\frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)=x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+y\operatorname{sin}⁡x,$ our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=\frac{\pi }{2}.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(\frac{\pi }{2},0)$ can be computed as follows:

$$
t(\frac{\pi }{2},0)={f}_{y}(\frac{\pi }{2},0)i-{f}_{x}(\frac{\pi }{2},0)j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(\frac{\pi }{2},0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+y\operatorname{sin}⁡x)i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+y\operatorname{sin}⁡x)j \\  & =(-x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)i-(\operatorname{cos}⁡y+y\operatorname{cos}⁡x)j \\ t(\frac{\pi }{2},0) & =(-\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡0+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}))i-(\operatorname{cos}⁡0+0\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}))j \\  & =i-j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our tangent vector is $i-j.$

Consider the plane curve 2x3y2−4xy=1−3x. Find a tangent vector to that curve at the point (1,1).

decision.explanation: Write the curve as f(x,y)=2x³y²−4xy+3x=1. Then f_x=6x²y²−4y+3 and f_y=4x³y−4x, giving ∇f(1,1)=⟨5,0⟩. A tangent vector is ⟨f_y,−f_x⟩=⟨0,−5⟩=−5j.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: Consider the plane curve $2{x}^{3}{y}^{2}-4xy=1-3x.$ Find a tangent vector to that curve at the point $(1,1).$
after.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{3}{y}^{2}-4xy & =1-3x \\ 2{x}^{3}{y}^{2}-4xy+3x & =1\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)=2{x}^{3}{y}^{2}-4xy+3x$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=0.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(1,1)$ can be computed as follows:

$$
t(1,1)={f}_{y}(1,1)i-{f}_{x}(1,1)j
$$

 

So, we calculate $t(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2{x}^{3}{y}^{2}-4xy+3x)i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{3}{y}^{2}-4xy+3x)j \\  & =(4y{x}^{3}-4x)i-(6{x}^{2}{y}^{2}-4y+3)j \\ t(1,1) & =(4(1)(1)^{3}-4(1))i-(6(1)^{2}(1)^{2}-4(1)+3)j \\  & =-5\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our tangent vector is $-5\,j.$

after.problem: Consider the plane curve ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=2xy+9.$ Find a tangent vector to that curve at the point $(-1,2).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =2xy+9 \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2xy-9 & =0\end{aligned}

If we set $f(x,y)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2xy-9$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=0.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(-1,2)$ can be computed as follows:

A tangent vector to the level curve that passes through the point (−1,2) can be computed as follows: t(−1,2)=fy(−1,2)i−fx(−1,2)j

content.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =2xy+9 \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2xy-9 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2xy-9$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=0.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(-1,2)$ can be computed as follows:

$$
t(-1,2)={f}_{y}(-1,2)\,i-{f}_{x}(-1,2)\,j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(-1,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2xy-9)\,i-\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2xy-9)\,j \\  & =(2y-2x)\,i-(2x-2y)\,j \\ t(-1,2) & =(2(2)-2(-1))\,i-(2(-1)-2(2))\,j \\  & =6\,i+6\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our tangent vector is $6\,i+6\,j.$

after.name: Question 9
after.problem: Consider the plane curve $2x\operatorname{ln}⁡y=8xy+2-8e.$ Find a tangent vector to that curve at the point $(1,e).$
after.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =8xy+2-8e \\ 2x\operatorname{ln}⁡y-8xy & =2-8e\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)=2x\operatorname{ln}⁡y-8xy$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=2-8e.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(1,e)$ can be computed as follows:

$$
t(1,e)={f}_{y}(1,e)\,i-{f}_{x}(1,e)\,j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(1,e):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x\operatorname{ln}⁡y-8xy)\,i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x\operatorname{ln}⁡y-8xy)\,j \\  & =(\frac{2x}{y}-8x)i-(2\operatorname{ln}⁡y-8y)\,j \\ t(1,e) & =(\frac{2(1)}{e}-8(1))i-(2\operatorname{ln}⁡e-8(e))\,j \\  & =(\frac{2}{e}-8)i+(8e-2)j\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, our tangent vector is $(\frac{2}{e}-8)i+(8e-2)\,j.$

decision.explanation: Set f(x,y)=xe^(y²+1)+y. Then f_x(1,0)=e and f_y(1,0)=1. A tangent vector is ⟨f_y,−f_x⟩=⟨1,−e⟩, giving option a.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem: Consider the plane curve $x{e}^{{y}^{2}+1}=e-y.$ Find a tangent vector to that curve at the point $(1,0).$
after.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x{e}^{{y}^{2}+1} & =e-y \\ x{e}^{{y}^{2}+1}+y & =e\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)=x{e}^{{y}^{2}+1}+y,$ our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=e.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(1,0)$ can be computed as follows:

$$
t(1,0)={f}_{y}(1,0)i-{f}_{x}(1,0)j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(1,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{e}^{{y}^{2}+1}+y)i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{e}^{{y}^{2}+1}+y)j \\  & =(2xy{e}^{{y}^{2}+1}+1)i-{e}^{{y}^{2}+1}\,j \\ t(1,0) & =(2(1)(0){e}^{0+1}+1)i-{e}^{0+1}\,j \\  & =i-e\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our tangent vector is $i-e\,j.$

before.html:
Question 11
?

At which points on the curve x2+y2=2y−2x is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector −i+j?

a
(−2,0) only
b
(0,0) only
c
(0,2) only
d
(−2,2) and (0,0)
e
(−2,0) and (0,2)
Submit

decision.explanation: For f(x,y)=x²+y²−2y+2x, a tangent vector is ⟨2y−2,−2x−2⟩. Its dot product with ⟨−1,1⟩ is −2(x+y), so perpendicularity requires y=−x. Substituting into the curve gives 2x²=−4x, hence x=0 or −2. The points are (0,0) and (−2,2).

after.problem: At which points on the curve ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=2y-2x$ is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector $-i+j?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =2y-2x \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2x-2y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2x-2y,$ our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=0.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows:

$$
t(x,y)={f}_{y}(x,y)\,i-{f}_{x}(x,y)\,j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & ={f}_{y}(x,y)\,i-{f}_{x}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2x-2y)\,i-\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2x-2y)\,j \\  & =(2y-2)\,i-(2x+2)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to $-i+j,$ we must have $t\cdot (-i+j)=0.$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y)\cdot (-i+j) & =0 \\ ((2y-2)\,i-(2x+2)\,j)\cdot (-i+j) & =0 \\ -(2y-2)-(2x+2) & =0 \\ -2y-2x & =0 \\ y & =-x\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $y=-x$ into the equation of our curve gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =2y-2x \\ {x}^{2}+(-x)^{2} & =2(-x)-2x \\ 2{x}^{2} & =-4x \\ 2{x}^{2}+4x & =0 \\ 2x(x+2) & =0 \\ x & =-2,0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally:

- For $x=-2,$ we get $y=2,$ and the corresponding point is $(-2,2).$

- For $x=0,$ we get $y=0,$ and the corresponding point is $(0,0).$

Question 11

At which points on the curve x2+y2=2y−2x is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector −i+j?

a
(−2,0) only
b
(0,0) only
c
(0,2) only
d
(−2,2) and (0,0)
e
(−2,0) and (0,2)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we bring all variables to one side: x2+y2=2y−2xx2+y2+2x−2y=0

If we set f(x,y)=x2+y2+2x−2y, our curve can be viewed as the level curve f(x,y)=0.

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows: t(x,y)=fy(x,y)i−fx(x,y)j

So, we calculate t(x,y): t(x,y)=fy(x,y)i−fx(x,y)j=∂∂y(x2+y2+2x−2y)i−∂∂x(x2+y2+2x−2y)j=(2y−2)i−(2x+2)j

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to −i+j, we must have t⋅(−i+j)=0.

t(x,y)⋅(−i+j)=0((2y−2)i−(2x+2)j)⋅(−i+j)=0−(2y−2)−(2x+2)=0−2y−2x=0y=−x

Substituting y=−x into the equation of our curve gives x2+y2=2y−2xx2+(−x)2=2(−x)−2x2x2=−4x2x2+4x=02x(x+2)=0x=−2,0.

Finally:

  • For x=−2, we get y=2, and the corresponding point is (−2,2).

  • For x=0, we get y=0, and the corresponding point is (0,0).

verification.explanation: The tangent vector ⟨2y−2,−2x−2⟩ is perpendicular to ⟨−1,1⟩ exactly when x+y=0. Substituting y=−x into the curve gives 2x(x+2)=0, yielding (−2,2) and (0,0). This confirms option d and the revealed solution; the incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option e.
